analysis.expert: Expert diagnostics, validation, provenance, and downloads
analysis.descriptiveIntro: Observed totals and missingness describe the published data; they do not identify causes or fraud.
analysis.deterministicIntro: These records come from arithmetic, identity, coverage, or documentary rules. Statistical previews contribute zero public priority points.
analysis.peerIntro: The peer detector compares eligible mesas under the registered leave-one-out method. It remains a research preview until independent validation passes.
analysis.spatialIntro: Spatial analysis stays non-evaluable until authenticated coordinates and a deterministic crosswalk are available.
analysis.outcomeIntro: Outcome sensitivity is separate from statistical signals and is unavailable until documentary trust and two-reviewer prerequisites pass.
analysis.expertIntro: Inspect model diagnostics, validation, provenance hashes, immutable artifacts, and replay resources.
analysis.noPeer: No peer-distribution result is published for this context.
analysis.noSpatial: No spatial result is published for this context.
analysis.errorBody: Missing or offline resources are not replaced with zeros or sample conclusions.
analysis.empty: No published records match this filter.

claims.title: What people are saying
claims.intro: These are the claims about the result that circulate most. Each carries the short answer, the method behind it, and — where one exists — the exact figure that confirms or contradicts it. Two of them cannot be answered with what this site holds, and say so.

lead.claim: «The pre-count and the official result did not match.»
lead.answer: There were small differences: the scrutiny adjusted some figures from the pre-count. The Registraduría reported 99.97% correspondence between the pre-count and the official result. A figure being corrected between the quick count and the reviewed scrutiny is not an anomaly — it is the procedure doing its job.
lead.method: The layers are kept separate and each figure keeps its version, source and legal status. The pre-count shown here is informational; the CNE's scrutiny is what certifies the result.
lead.figureAlt: 99.97% correspondence between the pre-count and the official result
lead.figureNote: The certified result matched the pre-count by 99.97%. The national margin between the two tickets was about 251,854 votes.

atypical.answer: Atypical does not mean impossible. A table can diverge from its neighbours for social, economic or precinct-composition reasons, and that is exactly why a statistical deviation only serves to have a person look at it.
atypical.detail: The peer comparison uses an empirical-Bayes beta-binomial model that excludes the table being evaluated, with a minimum denominator of 80 and groups of 30 peers. Predictive tail ≤ 0.001, Benjamini–Yekutieli q ≤ 0.05 and absolute residual ≥ 3.5 must all hold at once. Altogether that adds at most 10 of 100 points to the review-priority score.

benford.answer: It is not used, and the exclusion is deliberate. Votes per table are bounded by the number of voters, and in that range Benford produces false positives even in clean elections.
benford.detail: It is explicitly excluded from the score. The tests that are used require integer counts, their own denominators, and a single conservative correction for multiple comparisons over a hypothesis family fixed before looking at the data.

reportOrder.answer: Tables do not arrive in random order: small urban ones close and transmit first. That the trend shifts while the count is still coming in is geography, not manipulation.
reportOrder.detail: Reporting order, late changes and the timing of a revision are descriptive and score zero: they do not feed the review-priority score. The night's six bulletins are published with their timestamp and their hash so anyone can reconstruct the sequence.

moreVotesThanRegistered.verdict: Claim · not answerable with the data available
moreVotesThanRegistered.claim: “There are more votes than registered citizens.”
moreVotesThanRegistered.answer: If that shows up, it is an accounting failure and it heads the review queue. But in this table-level data the registered-voter denominator is not published, so this cannot be affirmed or denied here.
moreVotesThanRegistered.detail: Voter-roll limits are validated only when the field exists in the source. The states unknown, unavailable and not_applicable are distinct from one another and none is filled in with zero. An impossible count between fields that are present scores 100.

unavailable.verdict: Claim · not answerable with the data available
unavailable.answer: This claim is about voter-roll registration, which happens months before the count. Answering it would require the electoral roll, a source this site does not hold in its catalogue. Until it exists, the field is reported as unavailable, which is not the same as zero.
unavailable.detail: A new official source with its own legal status, grain and fingerprint. The states unknown, unavailable and not_applicable are distinct from one another and none is filled in with zero.
unavailable.figureAlt: An empty hexagon: the electoral roll is unavailable
unavailable.figureNote: Not a single hexagon: there is not one electoral-roll record in this catalogue.

crossChecked.title: What a newsroom checked, on its own
crossChecked.intro: The claims above were also examined by Detector de Mentiras, the fact-checking desk of La Silla Vacía — a newsroom independent of this project. We share no data, no code and no drafts with them: they reached their conclusions by their route and this site reached its own by another. They are linked here because agreeing separately is worth more than agreeing together. None of the ratings below is a finding of this site; each is the verdict they published under their own name.
crossChecked.sourceLabel: La Silla Vacía · Detector de Mentiras
crossChecked.linkNote: Links open lasillavacia.com in a new tab. The articles are in Spanish.

runs.claim: “Streaks of consecutive tables within a polling place prove the result was predetermined.”
runs.answer: This repository computes that same test. Its replication module runs a Wald–Wolfowitz runs test over consecutive tables within each polling place, and its own code marks every result as a neutral research association: never as evidence of fraud or vote injection, and never eligible for public audit-priority points. La Silla Vacía examined the same claim by its own method and published an equivalent conclusion, rated “Falso” (false).
runs.method: The replication is preregistered: within-place block permutation, max-T synchronised across year, round and municipality, and a seed derived from the data rather than chosen by whoever runs it — so nobody can re-draw until a preferred p-value appears. Tables inside a polling place are numbered by ID-number ranges, so their order is already correlated with voter age; a streak therefore measures association with that ordering, not a cause. Comparison against 2018 or 2022 is kept as context and is not accepted as an integrity signal.
runs.linkTitle: “Rachas en puestos no prueban fraude como dijo Petro y sucedieron en 2022”

forms.claim: “E-14 forms with crossings-out prove votes were altered in the runoff.”
forms.answer: A crossing-out on a tally sheet is a correction written by hand, and a written correction is the opposite of an erased trace. This site does not pick which figure is the real one: it keeps the layers apart — the informational pre-count and the scrutiny, which is what certifies — and keeps each one's version, source and legal status, so the difference stays visible. La Silla Vacía traced the circulating sheets back to their originals and rated the claim “Falso” (false).
forms.method: The layers are never collapsed into one number. When two layers differ, both are published with their version and their fingerprint, and the discrepancy is reported as a discrepancy rather than settled by choosing the more convenient figure.
forms.linkTitle: “Formularios E-14 no prueban fraude a favor de De la Espriella en segunda vuelta”

viralChart.claim: “A graphic shows who really won, once the irregular votes are subtracted from the total.”
viralChart.answer: Subtracting four figures drawn from four separate allegations from a national total does not produce a recount; it produces a subtraction. None of those figures comes from the same table-level count as the total they are taken from, so the answer depends entirely on what one decides to subtract. Here a total only exists by summing tables, each with its source and version. La Silla Vacía followed the graphic's four figures back to their origins and rated it “Falso” (false).
viralChart.method: Every national aggregate is rebuilt from the tables that compose it and can be recomputed from the same artefact. Adjustments applied straight to a total, with no per-table source behind them, are not accepted.
viralChart.linkTitle: “Gráfica viral impulsa narrativa de fraude con datos falsos a favor de Cepeda”

lawsuit.claim: “The annulment lawsuit and the evidence page that accompanies it show what happened.”
lawsuit.answer: This site does not analyse lawsuits: court filings are not in its catalogue, and it is not this site's place to say what a legal document proves. What it can say is that the digital-traceability questions that debate raises are exactly the questions an artefact carrying its version, source and fingerprint lets anyone answer without relying on somebody's reading. La Silla Vacía did review both texts and published its account of what they show and of what the texts themselves concede they do not.
lawsuit.method: Every figure published here carries its version, source, legal status and fingerprint, and every bulletin keeps its own. A traceability question is answered by recomputing the artefact, not by arguing about a screenshot.
lawsuit.linkTitle: “Ni la demanda de Petro ni su página de "pruebas" muestran fraude contra Cepeda”

timestamps.claim: “The timestamp and the hash lock on the E-14s reveal that the tally sheets were tampered with.”
timestamps.answer: A timestamp and a hash establish that a file has not changed since it was published. That is a real guarantee and a narrow one: on its own it describes nothing about what happened before the seal. That is why the night's six bulletins each keep their time and their fingerprint here — so anyone can repeat the check instead of trusting that we ran it. La Silla Vacía went through the post-runoff allegations one at a time and found no support for them.
timestamps.method: Reporting order, late changes and the timing of a revision are descriptive and score zero: they do not feed the review-priority score. What is fixed is each bulletin's fingerprint, which lets the published sequence be reconstructed.
timestamps.linkTitle: “Petro lanza nuevas denuncias de fraude sin sustento tras segunda vuelta”

attribution.claim: “A well-known journalist concluded that the evidence presented proves the fraud.”
attribution.answer: This claim is not about the data but about who said what, and this site has no way to answer it: its catalogue holds tally sheets and aggregates, not public statements. An attributed quote is checked against the original recording — that is reporting work, not statistics. La Silla Vacía looked for the record and rated the attribution “Falso” (false).
attribution.method: None: the field does not exist in this catalogue. Saying so is better than stretching a source until it appears to answer something it was never published to answer.
attribution.linkTitle: “Coronell no ha concluido que las pruebas de Petro comprueban el fraude electoral”

comparison.introA: The only way to answer that is to measure 2018 and 2022 with the same code and look at all three together. You will never see the 2026 number alone here, because a number alone means nothing.

thermometer.lead: These tests produce numbers that are alarming even in perfectly clean elections.
thermometer.body: It is like a temperature. 37.2 is alarming until you learn the person next to you read 38.5 and was healthy. That is why 2026 always appears beside 2018 and 2022, measured with the same thermometer.

legend.1: The grey band is what was already seen in 2018 and 2022.
legend.2: Each dot is one election. All three are equal on purpose: none carries more weight.
legend.3: If the 2026 dot falls inside the band, it resembles what came before. If it falls outside, it does not.

digitUniformity.plainLabel: Do the last digits of each count come out even?
digitUniformity.human: If someone invented the counts, the last digits would tend to repeat. The test measures whether they come out even.
digitUniformity.plainReading: All three elections exceed the threshold, and 2022 exceeds it by more than 2026 does. That is precisely why this number, alone, says nothing.
digitUniformity.techReading: 2018 30.17 · 2022 55.72 · 2026 35.52, critical value 16.92. 2026 sits below 2022, inside the range already observed.
digitUniformity.plainCritLabel: here the test says “look at this”

unanimousMesas.plainLabel: How many tables voted entirely for one candidate?
unanimousMesas.human: A unanimous table is one where the other candidate received exactly zero. Blank, null and unmarked ballots are not candidate votes.
unanimousMesas.plainReading: In 2026 it was 0.627 per 100 tables, more than 2018 or 2022. Still small, but above what was seen before, so it warrants human review.
unanimousMesas.techReading: 0.354% in 2018 · 0.504% in 2022 · 0.627% in 2026. A descriptive observation: it orders a look, it concludes nothing.

benford.label: What about Benford's law, which fails in all three?
benford.box: there is nothing to compare here
benford.body: This test is not built for counting votes: tables vary too widely in size, and that breaks it. It fails in all three elections, even the ones nobody disputes. We publish it anyway, because hiding it would look worse — but we do not draw it a band, because comparing it would not mean anything.

comparison.outsideVerdict: 2026 falls outside what was seen before
comparison.footnote: Computed with the same code over all three elections: 97,644 tables in 2018, 103,363 in 2022 and 122,020 in 2026. 2026 is the pre-count; 2018 and 2022 are the MMV table annex, different stages of the count.

process.title: How a vote reaches this page
process.intro: Nine steps between the official document and the hexagon you see above. Three of them are gates: if they are not cleared, nothing is published — not even partially. The site prefers to say nothing over saying something it cannot support.
process.footnote: All the code that runs these nine steps is public, and anyone can run it over the same sources and get the same result. If that were not possible, the site would have nothing to offer that a press release does not already offer.

01.title: Source catalog
01.body: Before anything is downloaded, the official sources that exist are declared, with their legal status and their granularity. The Registraduría publishes the pre-count and the scrutiny; the CNE declares and certifies. A source not in the catalog does not enter the site.

02.title: Collection with a fingerprint
02.body: Each file is fetched from its official address and stored with the exact retrieval time and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the content as it arrived. Nothing is edited along the way.

03.title: Reading without filling gaps
03.body: A reader translates each format into a common structure. Where the source does not publish a value, it stays unknown or unavailable. No gap is ever turned into a zero.

04.title: Arithmetic validation
04.body: It is checked that counts are non-negative integers, that table identities are canonical, and that each source's own sums close. Voter-roll limits are validated only when the field exists.
04.art: If a source's arithmetic does not close, that source is not published.

05.title: Reconciliation across layers
05.body: The same field, at the same table, at the same granularity, is compared across pre-count, E-14 acta and scrutiny. What does not match is recorded as a documentary difference, with its verification.

06.title: Declared coverage
06.body: What was and was not collected is measured, separating missing, ambiguous and excluded. Coverage is published as part of the result, not as a footnote.
06.art: Without clearing the coverage gate, there is no publication.

07.title: Historical baseline
07.body: The same code is run over 2018 and 2022 to have something to compare against. A single year's figure is never published alone, because alone it means nothing.

08.title: Human review
08.body: Wording, personal data and the correction for multiple comparisons are reviewed before any signal goes out. No conclusion is issued about intent or responsibility.

09.title: Immutable version
09.body: The publication is frozen with its version, its fingerprint, its declared schema and its OpenAPI contract. Reverting is not editing: it is moving a pointer to another version.

log.intro: The order in which the decisions were made matters as much as the result. Several of the ones here — separating the layers, not filling the gaps, excluding Benford — were made before looking at the 2026 data, which is why they hold up afterward.
log.note: Project record · dates verifiable in version history
log.trackHint: The timeline advances as you scroll the page; each milestone appears on the curve as it is reached.
